1.why: All seven screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary headings and teal action buttons are visually prominent, though the persistent warning box and logs compete somewhat for attention.

3.why: The linear single-card flow and clear step titles make the next required action easy to locate on each screen.

4.why: The user must recall and re-enter a long recovery token, a complex password policy, and a separate MFA code across multiple steps.

5.why: No password-manager hooks, autofill affordances, or “remember me” controls appear on any screen.

6.why: Nothing in the UI surfaces previously saved contacts, passwords, or familiar account identifiers for recognition.

7.why: Labels and instructions are mostly concise and readable, although the repeated security warning paragraph is lengthy.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the seven screenshots, so their helpfulness cannot be verified.

9.why: Password rules are stated as text only; no input examples, format masks, or illustrative samples are provided.

10.why: The flow offers only a single password-reset path; no alternative choices such as code or face login are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains at most one primary action and one or two fields, avoiding any overload of simultaneous choices.

12.why: Explicit confirmation screens and updating log entries clearly state the outcome after every major action.

13.why: Short instructional sentences appear on most steps, yet dedicated contextual tips or help links are absent.

14.why: Fields can be re-edited before submission, but no explicit “try again” or back navigation controls are visible.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style, warning box, and logs remain identical across all seven steps, supporting consistent learning.
